record.original_question: If a completion procedure is allowed to change the ordering during the run, using at each step an ordering that orients the current rules but not necessarily deleted old rules, can the procedure become incomplete, leaving persisting rules that are not confluent?

evidence.quote: Can completion be incomplete when the ordering is changed en route?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a Knuth–Bendix style completion procedure operating on a set of equations over a term algebra. In the standard setting, a fixed reduction ordering ≻ (a well-founded ordering on terms that is stable under contexts and substitutions) is chosen at the start, and every rule produced during the run is oriented according to ≻; the procedure is known to be correct in the sense that, if it does not fail and does not run forever, the persisting rules form a confluent and terminating term rewriting system equivalent to the input equations.

Now consider the following modification. At each step of the run, the procedure is allowed to choose a (possibly new) reduction ordering, with the only requirement that the chosen ordering orient the rules currently present in the system. Rules that have been deleted in earlier steps need not be oriented by the new ordering. Persisting rules are those rules that, once generated, are never deleted in the remainder of the run.

Question: Can this modified completion procedure be incomplete? That is, can a run of this procedure terminate (or persist) with a set of persisting rules that is terminating but not confluent, even though the run did not fail?
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been answered affirmatively: allowing the reduction ordering to change during a Knuth–Bendix completion run (requiring only that the current rules be oriented) renders the procedure incomplete. Even when the modified procedure terminates without failure, the resulting finite terminating term rewriting system can fail to be confluent. This is established in work on "About changing the ordering during Knuth-Bendix completion."

status_evidence.title: About changing the ordering during Knuth-Bendix completion
status_evidence.snippet: Modifying Knuth-Bendix completion so that the reduction ordering used for completion can be changed during completion (provided the new ordering is compatible with the actual rules) makes the algorithm incomplete.
status_evidence.claim: Permitting ordering changes during completion makes the procedure incomplete, even when it terminates without failure, since the resulting TRS may be non-confluent.
